description:
🔴 NEXT LIVE SESSION: Claude for Algo Trading, Tuesday 18 August, 7 PM IST. Watch Claude turn a plain-English trading idea into a systematic, testable strategy, live, with Ishan Shah and Sanya Modi. Register Here: https://bit.ly/4g0hwkP Dr. Ernest Chan is a part of our faculty board in our Executive Programme in Algorithmic Trading (EPAT).

In this video he addresses the question:
- Where do I start?
- What models should I explore (simple modes/deep learning)?
- What preprocessing is required for simple models/deep learning models? 
- Using Deep Learning - I have read that using deep learning you can forecast based on other time series values (for example series tl and t2 help in forecasting required series t3), how to extend this for normal data? For example, if Trump tweets that trade war between the US and China is over, then the markets will improve in another X days. In this example, what President Trump tweets is not forecastable but still an independent event and causes the market to fluctuate. 

Don't forget to 'Like' and 'Share' this video and to 'Subscribe' to our YouTube channel!
-----------------------------------------
This video clip is from our webinar Machine Learning In Trading Q&A By Dr. Ernest Chan: https://youtu.be/m4BFOSaos7M

About the speaker:
Dr Chan is the Founder & CEO of PredictNow.ai Inc and a Managing Member of QTS Capital Management, LLC.

He has worked for various investment banks (Morgan Stanley, Credit Suisse, Maple) and hedge funds (Mapleridge, Millennium Partners, MANE) since 1997.

Dr Chan received his PhD in physics from Cornell University and was a member of IBM’s Human Language Technologies group before joining the financial industry. He was a co-founder and principal of EXP Capital Management, LLC, a Chicago-based investment firm.

Dr Chan is also the author of Quantitative Trading: How to Build Your Own Algorithmic Trading Business (Wiley), Algorithmic Trading: Winning Strategies and Their Rationale and his third and latest book is on Machine Trading: Deploying Computer Algorithms to Conquer the Markets.
